thread:
Jane (Acme): Hey team — we saw duplicated completions when our client reconnected through our corporate proxy. Two full responses were produced and billed. Anyone seen this pattern?
Oliver - CS: Hi Jane, can you paste the exact client reconnect flow? is this using the SSE endpoint? :thinking_face: 
Jane (Acme): Yes SSE. Briefly: client opens SSE, gets 1 chunk, proxy returns 502 on a keepalive check -> client reconnects immediately with same session token. After reconnect we got the rest of the stream *plus* a second full completion back.
Maya (eng-runtime): Hmm, that suggests resume+retry produced a fresh generation instead of resuming. Do you have headers/raw logs showing session/resume token and any idempotency key?
Jane (Acme): Logs: 
```
GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-redwood HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
Authorization: Bearer sk-cust-...
X-Session-Id: sess-9412
X-Client-Heartbeat: 45
```
On reconnect: 
```
GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-redwood HTTP/1.1
X-Session-Id: sess-9412
X-Resume-Offset: 160
```
Response snippets show: 
```
event: chunk
data: {"seq":161,"text":"...rest of output"}

# later another full output stream begins (seq resets)
event: chunk
data: {"seq":1,"text":"full answer..."}
```

Raj (eng-infra): Does the proxy mutate/terminate TCP in a way that hides 502 from client? If client didn't receive final 200+stream-close, it might have retried creating a new request without telling server to de-duplicate. Also check if proxy strips or rewrites the X-Idempotency-Key header.
Oliver - CS: Billing flagged two tokens for same user at that timeframe and opened a ticket. billing-bot: Billing note: Invoice candidate shows duplicate token usage at 2025-08-03T14:25:11Z and 14:25:13Z (same session_id). Logged for manual review.
Maya (eng-runtime): Repro hypothesis: when resume header is present but server's resume token map eviction occurs (or resume metadata is missing because the proxy terminated the initial connection before session commit), the runtime falls back to normal generation path and produces a new generation. If client then stitches both streams it's duplicate. We should look at the server logs for sess-9412 to see resume state at 14:25.
Jane (Acme): I can share dump. Also we don't set an explicit Idempotency-Key today; client expects resume to be safe.
Maya (eng-runtime): Action items: 1) Jane: share raw capture (preferably curl capture or tcpdump) 2) Raj: check proxy behavior for 502 & header rewriting, plus whether it buffers and retries transparently 3) I'll instrument runtime to log resume-lookup misses and generation-fallbacks for that session id and timeframe.
Raj (eng-infra): Quick config note: our customers behind enterprise proxies sometimes have intermediate retries at the proxy layer. If proxy retries a request at the TCP layer, the server sees two *new* connections with identical headers — without an idempotency key, server treats them as separate. Recommend adding guidance to our SSE docs to include an X-Idempotency-Key or suggest the client do exponential backoff before immediate reconnect.
Maya (eng-runtime): Also adding a short-term server-side mitigation: when a resume header is present and resume lookup fails, delay starting a full fresh generation by 150ms and emit a special SSE event `event: resume-miss` so smart clients can suppress duplicate rendering. Not a long-term fix but reduces races.
Jane (Acme): That would help. For repro I can simulate proxy-induced 502 and immediate reconnect.
Oliver - CS: I'll coordinate with billing to hold off automated adjustments until we confirm duplicate-generation repro. billing-bot: Flag 4321 - hold auto-refund pending investigation.
Maya (eng-runtime): Can you also check whether your client automatically re-sends cookies or drops X-Resume-Offset? If offset omitted server may decide to generate anew.
Jane (Acme): Confirmed client sends Resume-Offset. Proxy may drop some trailing bytes. I'll run tcpdump and post capture.
Raj (eng-infra): FYI deploy-bot reports a small runtime patch queued: `runtime: log resume-lookup-result for SSE` — going out to canary in 10m. deploy-bot: canary deploy started (rev: r-20250803-17).
Jane (Acme): Thanks all. Will post capture shortly. Really appreciate the fast triage. :pray:
Oliver - CS: Thanks Jane — we'll keep this thread updated. If we confirm duplicate charge we'll coordinate a manual credit and update docs with proxy guidance. :)
